name: Occidental-Voe
description: Rolling continents break around shallow seas, their interiors scored by magnetic pole anomalies. Beyond a nearby asteroid belt, the land runs to a horizon that feels hand-drawn.

The air carries ammonia and old snow, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts. Forests of black-leaved flora drink the dim light and exhale a scent like cold iron.
Local legend among spacers says the planet hums on a frequency just below hearing. Instruments confirm it. Nobody agrees on the source.
The charts mark this world in cautious amber. Those who ignore the marking tend to come back rich, changed, or not at all.
